_comment: Sign-off smoke test for shared Metabase report cards. After editing ANY card, run: node scripts/verify-report-live.js --manifest scripts/report-cards.manifest.json — every entry must return live, non-empty results or the edit is NOT signed off. Test the heaviest org for each card (biggest = worst case for timeouts). Add a card+org row here whenever a new shared card or large org is onboarded. org_ids come from the ORGS map in server.js; card UUIDs are the public UUIDs (SHARED_UUIDS / per-org mbUuid). TIMEOUTS: the default 60s is a tripwire, but the APP's real budget is 60s then a 120s retry (see FIRST_TIMEOUT/RETRY_TIMEOUT in server.js), so a card between those two still serves live data. Rows carrying an explicit timeout of 120 are pinned to the app's true ceiling, with the measurement in the label — a failure there means the card has passed what the app itself can survive, not that it was slow once. Do NOT raise a timeout without recording the measured number and the date.

A long window is the only shape that discriminates)

checks.note: ADDED 2026-08-31 with v6. This shared card had no manifest row at all, so a dropped column or a date tag reset to Text would have surfaced as a blank Programs tab. SENDS A WINDOW: it is the only card here using {{start_date}} outside an optional block, so Metabase enforces it and the card 400s with 'missing required parameters' however healthy it is — the same false alarm the health check had on _shared/programs. 7 DAYS is what the page itself requests; this card scales badly with the range (apex 2026-08-31: 7d 1,042 rows/57.8s, 14d 81.5s, 30d 104.5s, 90d timed out past 150s). TIMEOUT 180 = the app's own ceiling (60s first try + 120s retry): it answers in ~58s alone but has been seen to blow 120s inside a full sweep, and this card has measured 7.7s-59.8s on identical inputs, so a single slow run is not evidence of breakage. V6.1 HELPED BUT DID NOT FIX THIS, and the honest numbers are below. Measured at apex 2026-09-01 over the 7-day window the page sends, AFTER the v6.1 fold and Dan's tag flip: 124.0s (1,125 rows), then a 180s TIMEOUT on the very next run. So it answers now where it did not before, but it is still past the app's own ceiling (60s first try + 120s retry) and apex will keep serving Programs from cache with live refreshes failing. NOT SIGNED OFF. Where the time is NOT: the location CTEs v6.1 removed cost 4.7s (I earlier quoted 0.88s and then 9.8s — both wrong, the second because that probe ran its own extra COUNT(*) over sessions), and `slots` costs 10.2s. Both are small fractions of ~120s, so ROLLING v6 BACK WOULD NOT FIX THIS EITHER — a conclusion worth keeping, because rollback was the obvious lever and it is the wrong one. PRIME SUSPECT is `item_tx`: a correlated LATERAL over order_item_transaction for EVERY order_item the org has ever had, unwindowed. PARKED, DO NOT OPTIMISE FURTHER (Dan, 2026-09-01): "i think the solution here is 'don't worry about it', we'll address this when we move to an api direct model. No reason to optimize something now that won't be around soon." So this row is expected to time out at apex until that move, and a TIMEOUT here is NOT actionable. The row STAYS anyway, because it still catches the things that are: a dropped column, a date tag reset to Text, an unshared card. Consequence to expect: the manifest sweep reports 21/22 rather than 22/22 for this reason alone. TELL THE TWO FAILURES APART: a TIMEOUT here is the parked perf issue and is expected; "An error occurred. (HTTP 400)" is NOT — that is the date tags reset to Text by an API push, which only a human flipping them in the Metabase UI can clear. v7/v8 2026-09-01 appended eight more columns (autopay/manual plan items and value, past due, scheduled manual, scheduled auto-pay, no-plan balance), so this row now also guards those against a silent drop.

programs-monthly / apex (card 21055, ADDED 2026-09-01 — the money half of the Programs by-month panel. SIGNED OFF 2026-09-01: 12 rows in 1.9s for Sep 2025–Aug 2026, through the public endpoint with the app's own date/single parameters. Apex is the worst case: a full scan of materialized.item_log_report, measured 21.4s unfiltered all-time against the base-table join which TIMED OUT past 60s on a single month. If this row starts returning 'An error occurred.', the start_date/end_date tags have been reset to Text and the app's date/single parameters no longer match — only a human re-flipping them in the Metabase UI fixes that) — FIXED 2026-09-09: this row sent NO date parameters and had therefore been failing with missing-required-parameter since it was added on 2026-09-01. Card 21055 uses {{start_date}}/{{end_date}} BARE inside generate_series (they bound the month series, so they cannot drop out of an optional block), which is why a dateless probe refuses in 0.1s rather than timing out. days:365 not daysAhead: this is a BACKWARD monthly revenue rollup, and its own sign-off window was Sep 2025 -> Aug 2026. THIRD instance of the dateless-manifest-row bug, after card 17301 v7 and both programs-schedule rows.

waitlist / apex (card 19273 v6, ADDED 2026-09-01 — this shared card had NO manifest row at all, and its central number was wrong for months: a claim was inferred from a timestamp that really marked the expiry sweep. SIGNED OFF 2026-09-01: 3,374 rows in 13.0s through the public endpoint with the app's own date/single parameters. An 'An error occurred.' here means the Start/End Date tags were reset to Text by an API push and need re-flipping in the Metabase UI)

programs-schedule / apex (card 21649 — the heaviest org. daysAhead:7 is LOAD-BEARING: programs-schedule is in FORWARD_REPORTS and not in NO_DATE_REPORTS, so the app always sends today -> today+DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS(7). This row shipped 2026-09-08 with NO date parameters at all, which drops the card's optional [[ ]] blocks and asks for the org's ENTIRE HISTORY — it then timed out three times (120s, 200s, 200s) and read as a card regression it was not. Windowed the same afternoon: 801 rows in 93.0s. The unwindowed shape defeats the card's whole design, since every CTE joins FROM `win`. Same mistake already recorded in CLAUDE.md for card 17301 v7. NOTE 93.0s EXCEEDS the app's 60s first-try budget and falls to the 120s retry — pre-existing at apex, not caused by the Section First Session column, which was measured at +0.09s with an identical row count. An 'An error occurred.' here means an API push reset the date tags to Text)

programs-schedule / watertown (TIMEZONE regression case — an EASTERN org, pinned for the same reason smyrna is pinned on fasttrack: Metabase renders in America/Los_Angeles, so a Pacific org structurally cannot catch this class of bug. The card resolves each org's own majority location.timezone and converts before rendering Date/Day/Begin/End; watertown is America/New_York and the conversion moves every row three hours — a 6:00pm class reads 3:00pm without it, and an 8:00am class reads 5:00am, which slips a DAY at the window boundary. daysAhead:7, 38 rows in 28.1s on 2026-09-08. Without the window this row read 3,269 rows in 36.8s — the org's whole history, which is not what the app asks for)

roster / apex (card 17296 — the heaviest org, and THIS SHARED CARD HAD NO MANIFEST ROW AT ALL until 2026-09-09, so a lost column or a re-Texted date tag would have been discovered as a blank roster rather than caught. daysAhead:14 is LOAD-BEARING: roster is in FORWARD_REPORTS and the page's own default is ROSTER_DEFAULT_DAYS=14, so that is the window the app actually sends. Unwindowed this row would ask for the org's entire history — the mistake already recorded here for card 17301 v7 and card 21649. 3,819 rows in 23.6s on 2026-09-09. An 'An error occurred.' here means an API push reset the date tags to Text and the card is registering duplicate parameters; flip both to Date and re-save until the list is FIVE, not nine

roster / watertown (EASTERN, so it is a timezone regression case rather than a duplicate: card 17296 dates every row by org.config primaryTimezone, and Metabase renders in America/Los_Angeles — a Pacific org structurally cannot catch a conversion regression here. Same reasoning that pins smyrna on fasttrack and watertown on programs-schedule. 485 rows in 2.7s on 2026-09-09
